Originally, "good faith" was generally defined to mean only "honesty in fact 
in the conduct or transaction concerned," a purely subjective test. See former 
UCC § 1-201(19). But Article 2 also contained a special definition of "good 
faith" for merchants: ''honesty in fact and the observance of reasonable 
commercial standards of fair dealing in the trade." Former DCC § 2-
103(1)(b). When UCC Article 1 was revised

"merchant standard" of good faith in Article 2 was incorporated into the 
general definition of "good faith" in Al'ticle 1 and made applicable to all
